title: Smt. Shirin Samuel And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 12 October, 2020

paragraphs.text:
HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
 
 

?Court No. - 66
 

 
Case :- HABEAS CORPUS WRIT PETITION No. - 292 of 2020
 

 
Petitioner :- Smt. Shirin Samuel And 2 Others
 
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
 
Counsel for Petitioner :- Nitin Mukesh
 
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
 

 
Hon'ble J.J. Munir,J.

This petition has been filed by Smt. Shirin Samuel, wife of Danise Samuel, against the fourth respondent, asking this Court to issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of habeas corpus to order the first and the second petitioner, the two minor children of parties to be produced before this Court and set at liberty by entrusting them into the first petitioner's custody, their mother. The first petitioner and the fourth respondents were married according to Christian rites on 01.11.2007. Two children were born of the wedlock of parties. It appears that the matrimonial discordovertook the parties and they parted ways. The first petitioner and the fourth respondent have become an estranged couple. The fourth respondent filed for divorce before the Family Court, Kota, Rajasthan under Section 10 of the Indian Divorce Act. A decree dated 17.12.2019, has been passed by the Judge, Family Court, Kota, Rajasthan. It appears from the averments made in the petition that the first petitioner and the fourth respondents last resided together as a family at Kota, Rajasthan. They did not live together in the State of Uttar Pradesh. The parties turned an estranged couple in Rajasthan and were granted a decree for divorce by a Court in the State of Rajasthan. It is only that, that the first petitioner, who appears to be a native of district Rampur in Uttar Pradesh, came back to Uttar Pradesh and settled there. She has filed an FIR against her husband under Sections 498-A , 323 , 504 , 506 , IPC, at Police Station Patwai, District Rampur. That is permissible under the Code of Criminal Procedure . The facts do not show any transaction within the State of Uttar Pradesh, as may give rise to the whole or a part of the cause of action, in the State of Uttar Pradesh. The mere fact that the petitioner is domiciled in Uttar Pradesh, after a divorce would not confer territorial jurisdiction upon this Court to entertain this writ petition, asking for a writ or habeas corpus to be issued to a person claimed to be illegally detaining the petitioner Nos. 2 and 3, in a place beyond the territorial jurisdiction of this Court.
In this view of the matter, this Court is of opinion that there is no territorial jurisdiction with us to entertain this habeas corpus writ petition.
The petition is, accordingly, dismissed on the ground of lack of territorial jurisdiction.
It shall always be open to the petitioner to approach the Court of competent jurisdiction on the cause of action involved here.
